title: GluD1 modulates GluN2B-containing NMDAR function and plasticity at subicular synapses
title_zh: GluD1 调控亚齿状突触中GluN2B含有的NMDAR功能与可塑性
abstract: Dysregulation of the delta-type glutamate receptor GluD1 and N-methyl-D-aspartate receptors (NMDARs) is implicated in neuropsychiatric disorders including schizophrenia and intellectual disability, and GluD1 modulates NMDAR responses in hippocampal neurons. However, the precise mechanisms by which GluD1 influences specific NMDAR subtypes remain undefined, representing a critical gap given the reliance of synaptic plasticity and cognition on NMDAR composition. GluN2A- and GluN2B-containing NMDARs are essential for synaptic long-term potentiation (LTP) and contextual learning and memory. Here, we used CRISPR/Cas9 to generate GluD1 knockout (KO) in cultured hippocampal neurons and observed a selective decrease in GluN2B-containing NMDAR responses. In acute hippocampal slices, GluD1 KO similarly reduced GluN2B-containing NMDAR currents at ventral CA1→subiculum synapses and impaired LTP at these synapses. In vivo, region-specific GluD1 deficiency in the ventral subiculum disrupted long-term contextual memory, indicating a critical role for GluD1 in cognitive processes. These findings demonstrate that GluD1 is indispensable for preserving GluN2B-containing NMDAR function, synaptic plasticity, and memory, providing molecular insight into how GluD1 regulates NMDAR subtypes implicated in synaptic dysfunction in neuropsychiatric disorders. Understanding this mechanism will guide the development of therapeutic strategies that selectively target GluD1-dependent modulation of NMDAR subtypes in brain disease.
abstract_zh: δ型谷氨酸受体GluD1与N-甲基-D-天冬氨酸受体（NMDAR）的功能失调被认为与包括精神分裂症和智力障碍在内的神经精神疾病有关，且GluD1可调控海马神经元中的NMDAR反应。然而，GluD1如何影响特定NMDAR亚型的精确机制仍未明确，这在突触可塑性和认知依赖于NMDAR组成的背景下代表了一个关键的空白。GluN2A-和GluN2B含有的NMDAR对于突触长时程增强（LTP）和情境学习与记忆至关重要。在此，我们利用CRISPR/Cas9在培养的海马神经元中生成GluD1敲除（KO），并观察到GluN2B含有的NMDAR反应选择性下降。在 acute  hippocampal slices（ acute海马切片）中，GluD1 KO同样抑制了腹侧CA1→亚齿状突触中的GluN2B含有的NMDAR电流，并损害了这些突触的LTP。在体内，腹侧亚齿状区特异性GluD1缺乏破坏了长时程情境记忆，表明GluD1在认知过程中起关键作用。这些发现表明，GluD1对于维持GluN2B含有的NMDAR功能、突触可塑性和记忆至关重要，为GluD1如何调控在神经精神疾病中出现突触功能障碍的NMDAR亚型提供了分子见解。了解这一机制将指导开发选择性靶向GluD1调控NMDAR亚型的治疗策略。
